advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Note (comment or docstring) that AcliClient's cursor-stall protection lives in `_iter_cursor_pages`, since `_iter_pages`' `hasattr(client, 'next_page_token')` branch is inert for this client.
evidence: fetch_paging.py:129-132 iterates `("next_page_token", "nextPageToken")` and only reads them `if hasattr(client, attr)`
search of adapters/jira found no `next_page_token`/`nextPageToken` attribute set on AcliClient (only the local var inside `_iter_cursor_pages`)
fetch_paging.py:105-107 docstring still claims `_iter_pages` raises on same-token-twice
advisory.finding: `fetch_paging._iter_pages` performs same-token-twice cursor-stall detection by reading `client.next_page_token`/`client.nextPageToken` via `hasattr`, but `AcliClient` exposes no such attribute (the cursor now lives inside the generator held by `_SearchResult`). That client-level stall branch is therefore inert for AcliClient; the live protection is `_iter_cursor_pages`'s internal RunawayPaginationError. This is not a regression (the eager version also lacked the attribute) but the `_iter_pages` docstring/comment advertise a stall guard that never fires for this client, which is misleading for maintainers debugging a Cloud stall.

advisory.finding: The `empty_jira_search` fixture asserts `not thread.is_alive()` inside the `finally` block. If the test body (inside `yield`) raises, this assertion runs during unwind; a stuck server thread would raise an AssertionError that masks the original test failure's traceback, making triage harder.

ABSENCE: the handler validates only `self.path`, never the request body, so the fixture cannot distinguish a correctly-formed search from a degenerate one — it serves 200+empty for any body.
advisory.finding: `SearchHandler.do_POST` sends an empty `issues` page but omits any `Content-Length` handling for a non-POST or malformed body beyond reading declared length; it is correct for the empty-search contract, but it never asserts the request body actually contained the expected `jql`/`fields`, so a bridge caller that silently sends the wrong search body (e.g. empty JQL) would still be served a 200 and look healthy.

dropped.finding: `_SearchResult.pages` is populated with the per-issue iterator returned by `_iter_search_issues` (which does `yield from page["issues"]`), not a page iterator; the name `pages` and the `islice(cached.pages, ...)` usage read as paginating by page while they actually count individual issues. dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Preserve retryability of 429/5xx on the REST search read path (e.g. retry 429/5xx in _rest_urlopen_with_retry for the search call, or wrap search_issues in a 429-aware retry) so a rate-limited base search is not downgraded to an unretried terminal HTTPError that aborts the pass.
evidence: Primary failure: a transient Jira rate-limit (HTTP 429) / 5xx on the base JQL search read.

Old transport+disposition: `result = self._run(cmd, retry_on_timeout=True)  # READ — idempotent` (prior search_issues body, now deleted) routed through _run_acli, which 'Retries up to 2 times (3 total attempts) on CalledProcessError, with backoff' and aborts only on 401/assignee errors — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:543-546; a 429 non-zero exit was therefore RETRIED.

New transport+disposition: `_iter_search_issues(self._direct_rest_post_json, jql)` — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:482; _direct_rest_post_json uses `_rest_urlopen_with_retry(req, timeout=30)` — acli_rest.py:327; which 'Does NOT retry on ``urllib.error.HTTPError`` (4xx / 5xx)' and `except urllib.error.HTTPError: ... raise` — acli_rest.py:86-88,98-100.

New surfaced disposition confirmed by the regression test: a 429 is raised straight out of search_issues with no retry — tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_search_pagination.py:124-133 (`raise urllib.error.HTTPError(path, 429, 'rate limited', {}, None)` then `with pytest.raises(urllib.error.HTTPError): client.search_issues(...)`).

Caller that changes behavior: single-project base search fails CLOSED, re-raising the terminal HTTPError — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:556-557 (`if not _isolate_projects: raise`); the search READ path has no 429-retry classifier (the 429-is-retryable logic lives on the APPLY path only — src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:113-141).
dropped.finding: search_issues moved from the ACLI subprocess transport (which retried rate-limited/transient CalledProcessError reads up to 3x) to the REST transport whose _rest_urlopen_with_retry deliberately does NOT retry HTTPError, so a Jira 429 (or 5xx) on the base search now surfaces as an immediate, unretried urllib.error.HTTPError instead of a retried-and-recovered read.
scenarios: Jira Cloud returns 429 under rate-limit pressure during the base `fetch_snapshot` search for a single project — previously retried at the subprocess floor and usually succeeded; now aborts the pass with an unretried HTTPError.
Multi-project fetch: a 429 on one project's base search now degrades that project to skip+alert (fetcher.py:555-575) instead of retrying through the transient fault.
dropped.suggested_fix: Classify 429 (and transient 5xx) from the search read as retryable before it reaches fetch_snapshot: either add bounded Retry-After-aware retry for 429/503 inside _rest_urlopen_with_retry for the search path, or have _iter_search_issues/search_issues translate a 429 HTTPError into the same retryable disposition the subprocess read previously surfaced, so single-project base search no longer fails closed on a transient rate-limit.
